findings.text: Squire's browser server, as set-up installs it (@playwright/mcp 0.0.86, started by lay-down with no tool filter), offers browser_run_code_unsafe, which runs any code it is given, as text or from a named file, in the server's own process on the Mac, and browser_drop, which drops files from the Mac onto a page by their paths. The safety floor asks both like any browser call and does not refuse them (core/hooks/pre-tool-use.py lines 884 to 885, and the browser rule from line 1204), so on a yes the code runs or the file is sent, unchecked for the owner's details. Shown by calling each through the floor in a laid test world: code, code from a file, and a drop of the owner's profile file by its path are each asked, then made on the yes, while a script in the page and a file upload are refused. A red test would assert that, through the floor in the default mode and in auto mode, browser_run_code_unsafe in both forms and browser_drop with paths are refused, not asked, even after a yes. Smallest fix: add both to the browser tools refused yes or no, or refuse every browser tool the floor does not know it can check. Owning hand: the test author for the red test, then the builder.
